Emily —

Following our call this morning, attaching a draft MAP and an initial token-econ worksheet for the HelixMed evaluation. High level ask: we want to lock the evaluation acceptance criteria and the cost/unit checks before we spin up the PoC so procurement has clarity on expected spend and gating.

Key items I'm proposing for the MAP (short):
- Duration: 2-week PoC + 1 week of traffic soak for unit-econ measurement.
- Data: sample payloads (anonymized) and 10 representative user sessions (we only need token counts and prompt/response shapes).
- Traffic profile: peak QPS target (please confirm), % of long-context sessions (>1024 tokens), % repeat prompts (candidate for prefix/KV caching).
- Unit-econ inputs we need you to confirm: avg prompt tokens, avg response tokens, and expected monthly active MAUs hitting the assistant.

A few technical notes up front:
- We will measure tokens per interaction and produce a tokens-per-dollar projection using the model variants we discussed.
- Batching: dynamic batching reduces per-token compute at scale; we'll show projections at 10, 50, and 200 QPS.
- Caching: prefix + KV caching can materially cut token consumption for repeat flows — tell us expected repeat rate so we can model hit rates (we'll show 0%, 30%, 60% scenarios).

Attached: helix_map_draft_v2.pdf (MAP draft) and token-econ-sheet.xlsx (working numbers).

Next step: can you share one week of representative request logs (anonymized) or a small sample JSON of 10 sessions by EOD Thursday? That will let us populate the spreadsheet and run the cost sensitivity.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if useful.

Thanks for the note and the MAP draft. A few clarifying questions so our finance/procurement can model this internally:

1) Token accounting: do you normalize for tokenizer differences across model variants (we use a mix of short clinical queries and longer summary prompts)? Example: the same text tokenized differently across models could change tokens/$ by ~10-12%.
2) Caching & PHI: our legal team needs to confirm that caching prefix data won't persist identifiable health information. Can you confirm Redwood's default cache retention and options to disable or zero-out prefix storage for the PoC?
3) Typical session shapes: roughly 70% of our calls are short (<=128 tokens total) and 30% are a longer triage flow (avg 900 tokens) — is that sufficient for you to model hit rates?

Procurement note: we need a simple estimate per 10k calls at baseline (no caching), and the delta at 30% and 60% cache hit rates. Please send numbers we can put into our internal budget tool.

We'll try to compile an anonymized week of payloads — procurement will coordinate.

Karthik / Ben —

I pulled together an initial set of sanity checks and a short checklist to include in the MAP. Dropping the main math here so procurement has something actionable quickly. I'll attach the working sheet but also paste the important cells.

Assumptions we will show in the sheet (examples):
- Model baseline cost: $0.0025 per 1K tokens (model variant A) and $0.0012 per 1K tokens (quantized variant B) — we will include both for comparison.
- Session shapes "short" = 1 prompt (40 tokens) + 1 response (80 tokens) => 120 tokens/session.
- Session shapes "long" = 1 prompt (450 tokens) + 1 response (450 tokens) => 900 tokens/session.

Example per-10k-calls math (no caching):
- Baseline tokens = (0.7 * 120 + 0.3 * 900) * 10,000 = (84 + 270) * 10,000 = 3,540,000 tokens.
- Cost @ model A = 3,540,000 / 1000 * $0.0025 = $8.85.
- Cost @ model B = 3,540,000 / 1000 * $0.0012 = $4.25.

Caching scenarios (affects response tokens primarily):
- Hit rate 30%: effective tokens = baseline tokens * (1 - 0.30) => 2,478,000 tokens.
- Hit rate 60%: effective tokens = baseline tokens * (1 - 0.60) => 1,416,000 tokens.

Batching effects (latency tradeoffs):
- At low QPS (<=10) batching yields negligible token savings.
- At 50 QPS, batching window 20ms yields ~1.15x throughput improvement; at 200 QPS, continuous batching and kernel fusion can drive 1.4x token-efficiency on per-token CPU/GPU costs. We will show token-equivalent savings in the sheet as a multiplier applied to compute portion of cost.

Gating / acceptance criteria we recommend adding to MAP:
- Token accounting: measured tokens/session within +/-15% of the MAP projection across the PoC week.
- Cache behavior: achieve at least 25% visible prefix/KV hit rate on the representative traffic to consider caching part of the baseline.
- Latency: p95 generation <= 800ms for the chosen model variant under the PoC load profile.

Action items for Karthik:
- Ask HelixMed for the anonymized week of logs (Emily already agreed to send).
- Populate the token-econ-sheet with the real payloads and run the 0/30/60% cache simulations + batching multipliers.

I'll take the lead on the spreadsheet and produce a short slide with the three scenario outputs (no cache / 30% / 60%) by EOD Wednesday so procurement can slot numbers into their tool.
